t.4.59.1: Then the leaders of the monkey troops, seated on the inaccessible mountain, surrounded on all sides that vulture, who had bathed and offered the water libation.
t.4.59.3: Having made silence, let the monkeys listen to me with attentive minds. I shall truly declare how I know of Maithilī.
t.4.59.2: Sampāti, having won their trust, spoke again with joy to Aṅgada, who sat there surrounded by all those monkeys.
t.4.59.4: Long ago I fell onto the summit of this Vindhya, in the forest, my limbs engulfed by the heat of the sun, scorched by the sun's rays.
t.4.59.5: Regaining consciousness after six nights, helpless and as if reeling, I looked about in all directions but could recognize nothing at all.
t.4.59.6: Then, having surveyed the oceans, the mountains, all the rivers and lakes, the woods and the forest regions, a thought came to me.
t.4.59.7: Crowded with flocks of joyful birds, with caves, hollows and peaks, on the shore of the southern ocean, this was ascertained to be the Vindhya.
t.4.59.8: And here there was a holy hermitage, well honored even by the gods, in which there lived a sage named Niśākara, of fierce austerities.
t.4.59.9: O knowers of dharma, after the sage Niśākara had gone to heaven, I have dwelt in this place without that ṛṣi for eight thousand years.
t.4.59.10: Having descended slowly and with difficulty from the rugged summit of the Vindhya, I came back again in distress to the earth covered with sharp darbha grass.
t.4.59.11: I wish to see that sage, having come here with great difficulty and in deep sorrow; for he was often visited by Jaṭāyu and by me.
t.4.59.12: Near his hermitage fragrant breezes blew; no tree was to be seen that was not in blossom or that was without fruit.
t.4.59.14: Then I saw, standing not far off, a sage blazing with splendour, unassailable, who had performed his ablutions and was returning, his face turned toward the north.
t.4.59.13: Having reached the holy hermitage, I took shelter at the foot of a tree, and, eager to see the venerable Niśākara, I waited for him.
t.4.59.15: Bears, sṛmaras, tigers, lions, elephants and serpents surround him and approach him, as living beings approach one who gives.
t.4.59.16: Then, knowing that the sage had arrived, those creatures went away, just as the whole army together with the ministers departs once the king has gone in.
t.4.59.17: The sage, pleased on seeing me, went back into his hermitage; then, coming out after only a moment, he asked me what my purpose was.
t.4.59.19: Two vultures, equal to Mātariśvan in speed, were seen by me before: brothers, kings of the vultures, able to assume any form at will.
t.4.59.18: O gentle one, seeing the ruined state of your feathers, the cause is not understood: these two wings of yours are burnt by fire, and your skin too is covered with wounds.
t.4.59.20: You, Sampāti, are the elder, and Jaṭāyu is your younger brother. Taking on a human form, let him clasp my feet.
t.4.59.21: What is the cause of your affliction, and how did your wings fall away? Or by whom was this punishment inflicted upon you? Tell everything to me, who am asking.
